+# -*- coding: utf-8 -*-
+#
+# Modified version of gat_predictor.py to accomodate continuous node and edge features
+# Original version available at https://github.com/awslabs/dgl-lifesci/blob/master/python/dgllife/model/model_zoo/gat_predictor.py
+#
+# Copyright Amazon.com, Inc. or its affiliates. All Rights Reserved.
+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+#
+# GIN-based model for regression and classification on graphs.
+# pylint: disable= no-member, arguments-differ, invalid-name
+
+import torch
+import torch.nn as nn
+
+from .gat import GAT, WeightedSumAndMax
+
+__all__ = ["GATPredictor"]
+
+
+class GATPredictor(nn.Module):
+    r"""GAT-based model for regression and classification on graphs.
+
+    GAT is introduced in `Graph Attention Networks <https://arxiv.org/abs/1710.10903>`__.
+    This model is based on GAT and can be used for regression and classification on graphs.
+
+    After updating node representations, we perform a weighted sum with learnable
+    weights and max pooling on them and concatenate the output of the two operations,
+    which is then fed into an MLP for final prediction.
+
+    For classification tasks, the output will be logits, i.e.
+    values before sigmoid or softmax.
+
+    Parameters
+    ----------
+    node_in_feats : int
+        Size for the input node features.
+    edge_in_feats : int
+        Size for the input edge features.
+    hidden_feats : list of int
+        ``hidden_feats[i]`` gives the output size of an attention head in the i-th GAT layer.
+        ``len(hidden_feats)`` equals the number of GAT layers. By default, we use ``[32, 32]``.
+    num_heads : list of int
+        ``num_heads[i]`` gives the number of attention heads in the i-th GAT layer.
+        ``len(num_heads)`` equals the number of GAT layers. By default, we use 4 attention heads
+        for each GAT layer.
+    agg_modes : list of str
+        The way to aggregate multi-head attention results for each GAT layer, which can be either
+        'flatten' for concatenating all-head results or 'mean' for averaging all-head results.
+        ``agg_modes[i]`` gives the way to aggregate multi-head attention results for the i-th
+        GAT layer. ``len(agg_modes)`` equals the number of GAT layers. By default, we flatten
+        multi-head results for intermediate GAT layers and compute mean of multi-head results
+        for the last GAT layer.
+    activations : list of activation function or None
+        ``activations[i]`` gives the activation function applied to the aggregated multi-head
+        results for the i-th GAT layer. ``len(activations)`` equals the number of GAT layers.
+        By default, ELU is applied for intermediate GAT layers and no activation is applied
+        for the last GAT layer.
+    biases : list of bool
+        ``biases[i]`` gives whether to add bias for the i-th GAT layer. ``len(activations)``
+        equals the number of GAT layers. By default, bias is added for all GAT layers.
+    n_tasks : int
+        Number of tasks, which is also the output size. Default to 1.
+    predictor_hidden_feats : int
+        Size for hidden representations in the output MLP predictor. Default to 128.
+    predictor_dropout : float
+        The probability for dropout in the output MLP predictor. Default to 0.
+    """
+
+    def __init__(
+        self,
+        node_in_feats,
+        edge_in_feats,
+        n_layers=5,
+        hidden_feats=300,
+        num_heads=1,
+        dropout=0.1,
+        agg_mode="flatten",
+        activation=nn.functional.elu,
+        bias=True,
+        n_tasks=1,
+        predictor_hidden_feats=256,
+    ):
+        super(GATPredictor, self).__init__()
+
+        self.encoder = GAT(
+            node_in_feats=node_in_feats,
+            edge_in_feats=edge_in_feats,
+            n_layers=n_layers,
+            hidden_feats=hidden_feats,
+            num_heads=num_heads,
+            agg_mode=agg_mode,
+            activation=activation,
+            dropout=dropout,
+            bias=bias,
+        )
+
+        gnn_out_feats = hidden_feats
+
+        self.readout = WeightedSumAndMax(gnn_out_feats)
+
+        self.decoder = nn.Sequential(
+            nn.Linear(2 * gnn_out_feats, predictor_hidden_feats),
+            nn.ReLU(),
+            nn.Linear(predictor_hidden_feats, n_tasks),
+        )
+
+    def forward(self, g, node_feats, edge_feats):
+        """Graph-level regression/soft classification.
+
+        Parameters
+        ----------
+        g : DGLGraph
+            DGLGraph for a batch of graphs
+        node_feats : float32 tensor of shape (V, node_in_feats)
+            Input node features.
+        edge_feats : float32 tensor of shape (E, edge_in_feats)
+            Input edge features.
+
+        Returns
+        -------
+        FloatTensor of shape (B, n_tasks)
+            * Predictions on graphs
+            * B for the number of graphs in the batch
+        """
+        node_feats = self.encoder(g, node_feats, edge_feats)
+        graph_feats = self.readout(g, node_feats)
+        output = self.decoder(graph_feats)
+
+        return output

+# -*- coding: utf-8 -*-
+#
+# Modified version of gin.py
+# Original version available at https://github.com/awslabs/dgl-lifesci/blob/master/python/dgllife/model/gnn/gin.py

+from dgl.nn.pytorch import GINConv
+
+__all__ = ["GIN"]
+
+
+class GINLayer(nn.Module):
+    def __init__(self, in_feats, out_feats, activation=F.relu, dropout=0.1):
+        super(GINLayer, self).__init__()
+        self.mlp = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(in_feats, out_feats), nn.ReLU())
+        self.conv = GINConv(self.mlp)
+        self.activation = activation
+        self.dropout = nn.Dropout(dropout)
+
+    def reset_parameters(self):
+        for m in self.mlp:
+            if hasattr(m, "reset_parameters"):
+                m.reset_parameters()
+
+    def forward(self, g, node_feats, edge_feats=None):
+        h = self.conv(g, node_feats)
+        if self.activation is not None:
+            h = self.activation(h)
+        h = self.dropout(h)
+        return h
+
+
+class GIN(nn.Module):
+    def __init__(
+        self, node_in_feats, edge_in_feats, num_layers=5, emb_dim=300, dropout=0.1
+    ):
+        super(GIN, self).__init__()
+        self.project_node_feats = nn.Sequential(
+            nn.Linear(node_in_feats, emb_dim), nn.ReLU()
+        )
+        self.gnn_layers = nn.ModuleList(
+            [GINLayer(emb_dim, emb_dim, dropout=dropout) for _ in range(num_layers)]
+        )
+
+    def reset_parameters(self):
+        self.project_node_feats[0].reset_parameters()
+        for l in self.gnn_layers:
+            l.reset_parameters()
+
+    def forward(self, g, node_feats, edge_feats=None):
+        node_feats = self.project_node_feats(node_feats)
+        for l in self.gnn_layers:
+            node_feats = l(g, node_feats, edge_feats)
+        return node_feats

+# -*- coding: utf-8 -*-
+#
+# Modified version of pagtn.py
+# Original version available at https://github.com/awslabs/dgl-lifesci/blob/master/python/dgllife/model/gnn/pagtn.py

+#
+# Path-Augmented Graph Transformer Network
+# pylint: disable= no-member, arguments-differ, invalid-name
+
+import torch
+import torch.nn as nn
+from dgl.nn.functional import edge_softmax
+import dgl.function as fn
+
+__all__ = ["GTN"]
+
+
+class GTNLayer(nn.Module):
+    """
+    Single PAGTN layer from `Path-Augmented Graph Transformer Network
+    <https://arxiv.org/abs/1905.12712>`__
+
+    This will be used for incorporating the information of edge features
+    into node features for message passing.
+
+    Parameters
+    ----------
+    node_in_feats : int
+        Size for the input node features.
+    node_out_feats : int
+        Size for the output node features.
+    edge_feats : int
+        Size for the input edge features.
+    dropout : float
+        The probability for performing dropout. Default to 0.1
+    activation : callable
+        Activation function to apply. Default to LeakyReLU.
+    """
+
+    def __init__(
+        self,
+        node_in_feats,
+        node_out_feats,
+        edge_feats,
+        dropout=0.1,
+        activation=nn.LeakyReLU(0.2),
+    ):
+        super(GTNLayer, self).__init__()
+        self.attn_src = nn.Linear(node_in_feats, node_in_feats)
+        self.attn_dst = nn.Linear(node_in_feats, node_in_feats)
+        self.attn_edg = nn.Linear(edge_feats, node_in_feats)
+        self.attn_dot = nn.Linear(node_in_feats, 1)
+        self.msg_src = nn.Linear(node_in_feats, node_out_feats)
+        self.msg_dst = nn.Linear(node_in_feats, node_out_feats)
+        self.msg_edg = nn.Linear(edge_feats, node_out_feats)
+        self.wgt_n = nn.Linear(node_in_feats, node_out_feats)
+        self.dropout = nn.Dropout(dropout)
+        self.act = activation
+        self.reset_parameters()
+
+    def reset_parameters(self):
+        """Reinitialize learnable parameters."""
+        gain = nn.init.calculate_gain("relu")
+        nn.init.xavier_normal_(self.attn_src.weight, gain=gain)
+        nn.init.xavier_normal_(self.attn_dst.weight, gain=gain)
+        nn.init.xavier_normal_(self.attn_edg.weight, gain=gain)
+        nn.init.xavier_normal_(self.attn_dot.weight, gain=gain)
+        nn.init.xavier_normal_(self.msg_src.weight, gain=gain)
+        nn.init.xavier_normal_(self.msg_dst.weight, gain=gain)
+        nn.init.xavier_normal_(self.msg_edg.weight, gain=gain)
+        nn.init.xavier_normal_(self.wgt_n.weight, gain=gain)
+
+    def forward(self, g, node_feats, edge_feats):
+        """Update node representations.
+
+        Parameters
+        ----------
+        g : DGLGraph
+            DGLGraph for a batch of graphs
+        node_feats : float32 tensor of shape (V, node_in_feats) or (V, n_head, node_in_feats)
+            Input node features. V for the number of nodes in the batch of graphs.
+        edge_feats : float32 tensor of shape (E, edge_in_feats)
+            Input edge features. E for the number of edges in the batch of graphs.
+
+        Returns
+        -------
+        float32 tensor of shape (V, node_out_feats) or (V, n_head, node_out_feats)
+            Updated node features.
+        """
+
+        g = g.local_var()
+        # In the paper node_src, node_dst, edge feats are concatenated
+        # and multiplied with the matrix. We have optimized this step
+        # by having three separate matrix multiplication.
+        g.ndata["src"] = self.dropout(self.attn_src(node_feats))
+        g.ndata["dst"] = self.dropout(self.attn_dst(node_feats))
+        edg_atn = self.dropout(self.attn_edg(edge_feats)).unsqueeze(-2)
+        g.apply_edges(fn.u_add_v("src", "dst", "e"))
+        atn_scores = self.act(g.edata.pop("e") + edg_atn)
+
+        atn_scores = self.attn_dot(atn_scores)
+        atn_scores = self.dropout(edge_softmax(g, atn_scores))
+
+        g.ndata["src"] = self.msg_src(node_feats)
+        g.ndata["dst"] = self.msg_dst(node_feats)
+        g.apply_edges(fn.u_add_v("src", "dst", "e"))
+        atn_inp = g.edata.pop("e") + self.msg_edg(edge_feats).unsqueeze(-2)
+        atn_inp = self.act(atn_inp)
+        g.edata["msg"] = atn_scores * atn_inp
+        g.update_all(fn.copy_e("msg", "m"), fn.sum("m", "feat"))
+        out = g.ndata.pop("feat") + self.wgt_n(node_feats)
+        return self.act(out)
+
+
+class GTN(nn.Module):
+    """Multilayer PAGTN model for updating node representations.
+    PAGTN is introduced in `Path-Augmented Graph Transformer Network
+    <https://arxiv.org/abs/1905.12712>`__.
+
+    Parameters
+    ----------
+    node_in_feats : int
+        Size for the input node features.
+    node_out_feats : int
+        Size for the output node features.
+    node_hid_feats : int
+        Size for the hidden node features.
+    edge_feats : int
+        Size for the input edge features.
+    depth : int
+        Number of PAGTN layers to be applied.
+    nheads : int
+        Number of attention heads.
+    dropout : float
+        The probability for performing dropout. Default to 0.1
+    activation : callable
+        Activation function to apply. Default to LeakyReLU.
+    """
+
+    def __init__(
+        self,
+        node_in_feats,
+        node_out_feats,
+        node_hid_feats,
+        edge_feats,
+        depth=5,
+        nheads=1,
+        dropout=0.1,
+        activation=nn.LeakyReLU(0.2),
+    ):
+        super(GTN, self).__init__()
+        self.depth = depth
+        self.nheads = nheads
+        self.node_hid_feats = node_hid_feats
+        self.atom_inp = nn.Linear(node_in_feats, node_hid_feats * nheads)
+        self.model = nn.ModuleList(
+            [
+                GTNLayer(
+                    node_hid_feats, node_hid_feats, edge_feats, dropout, activation
+                )
+                for _ in range(depth)
+            ]
+        )
+        self.atom_out = nn.Linear(
+            node_in_feats + node_hid_feats * nheads, node_out_feats
+        )
+        self.act = activation
+
+    def reset_parameters(self):
+        """Reinitialize learnable parameters."""
+        gain = nn.init.calculate_gain("relu")
+        nn.init.xavier_normal_(self.atom_inp.weight, gain=gain)
+        nn.init.xavier_normal_(self.atom_out.weight, gain=gain)
+        self.model.reset_parameters()
+
+    def forward(self, g, node_feats, edge_feats):
+        """Update node representations.
+
+        Parameters
+        ----------
+        g : DGLGraph
+            DGLGraph for a batch of graphs
+        node_feats : float32 tensor of shape (V, node_in_feats)
+            Input node features. V for the number of nodes in the batch of graphs.
+        edge_feats : float32 tensor of shape (E, edge_in_feats)
+            Input edge features. E for the number of edges in the batch of graphs.
+
+        Returns
+        -------
+        float32 tensor of shape (V, node_out_feats)
+            Updated node features.
+        """
+        g = g.local_var()
+        atom_input = self.atom_inp(node_feats).view(
+            -1, self.nheads, self.node_hid_feats
+        )
+        atom_input = self.act(atom_input)
+        atom_h = atom_input
+        for i in range(self.depth):
+            attn_h = self.model[i](g, atom_h, edge_feats)
+            atom_h = torch.nn.functional.relu(attn_h + atom_input)
+
+        atom_h = atom_h.view(-1, self.nheads * self.node_hid_feats)
+        atom_output = torch.cat([node_feats, atom_h], dim=1)
+        atom_h = torch.nn.functional.relu(self.atom_out(atom_output))
+        return atom_h

+import torch
+import torch.nn as nn
+import torch.nn.functional as F
+from decimal import *
+from typing import Tuple
+
+
+# ----------------------------------------
+# >>>           encoder part           <<<
+# ----------------------------------------
+class MolConv3(nn.Module):
+    def __init__(self, in_dim, out_dim, point_num, k, remove_xyz=False):
+        super(MolConv3, self).__init__()
+        self.k = k
+        self.in_dim = in_dim
+        self.out_dim = out_dim
+        self.remove_xyz = remove_xyz
+
+        self.dist_ff = nn.Sequential(
+            nn.Conv2d(1, 1, kernel_size=1, bias=False),
+            nn.LayerNorm((1, point_num, k)),
+            nn.Sigmoid(),
+        )
+
+        if remove_xyz:
+            self.center_ff = nn.Sequential(
+                nn.Conv2d(in_dim - 3, in_dim + k - 3, kernel_size=1, bias=False),
+                nn.LayerNorm((in_dim + k - 3, point_num, k)),
+                nn.Sigmoid(),
+            )
+            self.update_ff = nn.Sequential(
+                nn.Conv2d(in_dim + k - 3, out_dim, kernel_size=1, bias=False),
+                nn.LayerNorm((out_dim, point_num, k)),
+                nn.Softplus(beta=1.0, threshold=20.0),
+            )
+        else:
+            self.center_ff = nn.Sequential(
+                nn.Conv2d(in_dim, in_dim + k, kernel_size=1, bias=False),
+                nn.LayerNorm((in_dim + k, point_num, k)),
+                nn.Sigmoid(),
+            )
+            self.update_ff = nn.Sequential(
+                nn.Conv2d(in_dim + k, out_dim, kernel_size=1, bias=False),
+                nn.LayerNorm((out_dim, point_num, k)),
+                nn.Softplus(beta=1.0, threshold=20.0),
+            )
+
+    def forward(
+        self, x: torch.Tensor, idx_base: torch.Tensor, mask: torch.Tensor
+    ) -> torch.Tensor:
+        # Generate features
+        dist, gm2, feat_c, feat_n = self._generate_feat(
+            x, idx_base, k=self.k, remove_xyz=self.remove_xyz
+        )
+        """Returned features: 
+		dist: torch.Size([batch_size, 1, point_num, k])
+		gm2: torch.Size([batch_size, k, point_num, k]) 
+		feat_c: torch.Size([batch_size, in_dim, point_num, k]) 
+		feat_n: torch.Size([batch_size, in_dim, point_num, k])
+		"""
+        feat_n = torch.cat(
+            (feat_n, gm2), dim=1
+        )  # torch.Size([batch_size, in_dim+k, point_num, k])
+        feat_c = self.center_ff(feat_c)
+        w = self.dist_ff(dist)
+
+        feat = w * feat_n + feat_c
+        feat = self.update_ff(feat)
+
+        # Average pooling along the fourth dimension
+        mask_expanded = (
+            mask.unsqueeze(1).unsqueeze(-1).expand_as(feat)
+        )  # [batch_size, out_dim, point_num, k]
+        feat = feat.masked_fill(~mask_expanded, 0.0)  # Set padding points to zero
+        valid_counts = mask.sum(dim=1, keepdim=True).clamp(
+            min=0.1
+        )  # Avoid division by zero
+        feat = feat.sum(dim=3) / valid_counts.unsqueeze(
+            2
+        )  # [batch_size, out_dim, point_num]
+        return feat
+
+    def _generate_feat(
+        self, x: torch.Tensor, idx_base: torch.Tensor, k: int, remove_xyz: bool
+    ) -> Tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
+        batch_size, num_dims, num_points = x.size()
+
+        # local graph (knn)
+        inner = -2 * torch.matmul(x.transpose(2, 1), x)
+        xx = torch.sum(x**2, dim=1, keepdim=True)
+        pairwise_distance = -xx - inner - xx.transpose(2, 1)
+        dist, idx = pairwise_distance.topk(k=k, dim=2)  # (batch_size, num_points, k)
+        dist = -dist
+
+        idx = idx + idx_base
+        idx = idx.view(-1)
+
+        x = x.transpose(
+            2, 1
+        ).contiguous()  # (batch_size, num_points, num_dims) -> (batch_size*num_points, num_dims)
+        # print('_double_gram_matrix (x):', torch.any(torch.isnan(x)))
+        graph_feat = x.view(batch_size * num_points, -1)[idx, :]
+        # print('_double_gram_matrix (graph_feat):', torch.any(torch.isnan(graph_feat)))
+        graph_feat = graph_feat.view(batch_size, num_points, k, num_dims)
+
+        # gram matrix
+        gm_matrix = torch.matmul(graph_feat, graph_feat.permute(0, 1, 3, 2))
+        gm_matrix = F.normalize(gm_matrix, dim=1)
+        # print('_double_gram_matrix (gm_matrix):', torch.any(torch.isnan(gm_matrix)))
+
+        # double gram matrix
+        sub_feat = gm_matrix[:, :, :, 0].unsqueeze(3)
+        sub_gm_matrix = torch.matmul(sub_feat, sub_feat.permute(0, 1, 3, 2))
+        sub_gm_matrix = F.normalize(sub_gm_matrix, dim=1)
+        # print('_double_gram_matrix (sub_gm_matrix):', torch.any(torch.isnan(sub_gm_matrix)))
+
+        x = x.view(batch_size, num_points, 1, num_dims).repeat(1, 1, k, 1)
+
+        if remove_xyz:
+            dist = dist.unsqueeze(3).permute(0, 3, 1, 2).contiguous()
+            gm2 = sub_gm_matrix.permute(0, 3, 1, 2).contiguous()
+            feat_c = x[:, :, :, 3:].permute(0, 3, 1, 2).contiguous()
+            feat_n = graph_feat[:, :, :, 3:].permute(0, 3, 1, 2).contiguous()
+        else:
+            dist = dist.unsqueeze(3).permute(0, 3, 1, 2).contiguous()
+            gm2 = sub_gm_matrix.permute(0, 3, 1, 2).contiguous()
+            feat_c = x.permute(0, 3, 1, 2).contiguous()
+            feat_n = graph_feat.permute(0, 3, 1, 2).contiguous()
+
+        return dist, gm2, feat_c, feat_n
+
+    def __repr__(self):
+        return (
+            self.__class__.__name__
+            + " k = "
+            + str(self.k)
+            + " ("
+            + str(self.in_dim)
+            + " -> "
+            + str(self.out_dim)
+            + ")"
+        )
+
+
+class Encoder(nn.Module):
+    def __init__(self, in_dim, layers, emb_dim, point_num, k):
+        super(Encoder, self).__init__()
+        self.emb_dim = emb_dim
+        self.hidden_layers = nn.ModuleList(
+            [
+                MolConv3(
+                    in_dim=in_dim,
+                    out_dim=layers[0],
+                    point_num=point_num,
+                    k=k,
+                    remove_xyz=True,
+                )
+            ]
+        )
+        for i in range(1, len(layers)):
+            if i == 1:
+                self.hidden_layers.append(
+                    MolConv3(
+                        in_dim=layers[i - 1],
+                        out_dim=layers[i],
+                        point_num=point_num,
+                        k=k,
+                        remove_xyz=False,
+                    )
+                )
+            else:
+                self.hidden_layers.append(
+                    MolConv3(
+                        in_dim=layers[i - 1],
+                        out_dim=layers[i],
+                        point_num=point_num,
+                        k=k,
+                        remove_xyz=False,
+                    )
+                )
+
+        self.conv = nn.Sequential(
+            nn.Conv1d(emb_dim, emb_dim, kernel_size=1, bias=False),
+            nn.LayerNorm((emb_dim, point_num)),
+            nn.LeakyReLU(negative_slope=0.2),
+        )
+
+    def forward(
+        self, x: torch.Tensor, idx_base: torch.Tensor, mask: torch.Tensor
+    ) -> torch.Tensor:
+        xs = []
+        for i, hidden_layer in enumerate(self.hidden_layers):
+            if i == 0:
+                tmp_x = hidden_layer(x, idx_base, mask)
+            else:
+                tmp_x = hidden_layer(xs[-1], idx_base, mask)
+            xs.append(tmp_x)
+
+        x = torch.cat(xs, dim=1)  # torch.Size([batch_size, emb_dim, point_num])
+        x = self.conv(x)
+
+        # Apply the mask: Set padding points to a very low value for max pooling and zero for average pooling
+        mask_expanded = mask.unsqueeze(1).expand_as(
+            x
+        )  # [batch_size, emb_dim, point_num]
+        x_masked_max = x.masked_fill(
+            ~mask_expanded, float("-inf")
+        )  # Replace padding with -inf for max pooling
+        x_masked_avg = x.masked_fill(
+            ~mask_expanded, 0.0
+        )  # Replace padding with 0 for average pooling
+
+        # Max pooling along the third dimension
+        max_pooled = torch.max(x_masked_max, dim=2)[0]  # [batch_size, emb_dim]
+
+        # Average pooling along the third dimension
+        # Count the valid (non-padding) points for each position
+        valid_counts = mask.sum(dim=1, keepdim=True).clamp(
+            min=0.1
+        )  # Avoid division by zero
+        avg_pooled = x_masked_avg.sum(dim=2) / valid_counts  # [batch_size, emb_dim]
+
+        x = max_pooled + avg_pooled
+        return x
+
+
+# ----------------------------------------
+# >>>           decoder part           <<<
+# ----------------------------------------
+class FCResBlock(nn.Module):
+    def __init__(self, in_dim: int, out_dim: int, dropout: float = 0.0) -> torch.Tensor:
+        super(FCResBlock, self).__init__()
+        self.in_dim = in_dim
+        self.out_dim = out_dim
+
+        self.linear1 = nn.Linear(in_dim, out_dim, bias=False)
+        self.bn1 = nn.LayerNorm(out_dim)
+
+        self.linear2 = nn.Linear(out_dim, out_dim, bias=False)
+        self.bn2 = nn.LayerNorm(out_dim)
+
+        self.linear3 = nn.Linear(out_dim, out_dim, bias=False)
+        self.bn3 = nn.LayerNorm(out_dim)
+
+        self.dp = nn.Dropout(dropout)
+
+    def reset_parameters(self):
+        self.linear1.reset_parameters()
+        self.linear2.reset_parameters()
+        self.linear3.reset_parameters()
+        self.bn1.reset_parameters()
+        self.bn2.reset_parameters()
+        self.bn3.reset_parameters()
+
+    def forward(self, x):
+        identity = x
+
+        x = self.bn1(self.linear1(x))
+        x = F.leaky_relu(x, negative_slope=0.2)
+        x = self.bn2(self.linear2(x))
+        x = F.leaky_relu(x, negative_slope=0.2)
+        x = self.bn3(self.linear3(x))
+
+        x = x + F.interpolate(identity.unsqueeze(1), size=x.size()[1]).squeeze()
+
+        x = F.leaky_relu(x, negative_slope=0.2)
+        x = self.dp(x)
+        return x
+
+    def __repr__(self):
+        return (
+            self.__class__.__name__
+            + " ("
+            + str(self.in_dim)
+            + " -> "
+            + str(self.out_dim)
+            + ")"
+        )
+
+
+# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# >>>                            Final model                            <<<
+# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
+class MolNet_RT(nn.Module):
+    def __init__(self, config):
+        super(MolNet_RT, self).__init__()
+        self.add_num = config["add_num"]
+        self.encoder = Encoder(
+            in_dim=int(config["in_dim"]),
+            layers=config["encode_layers"],
+            emb_dim=int(config["emb_dim"]),
+            point_num=int(config["max_atom_num"]),
+            k=int(config["k"]),
+        )
+        self.decoder = nn.Sequential(
+            FCResBlock(
+                in_dim=int(config["emb_dim"] + config["add_num"]),
+                out_dim=config["decode_layers"][0],
+            ),
+            *[
+                FCResBlock(
+                    in_dim=config["decode_layers"][i],
+                    out_dim=config["decode_layers"][i + 1],
+                    dropout=(
+                        config["dropout"]
+                        if len(config["decode_layers"]) - i <= 3
+                        else 0.0
+                    ),
+                )
+                for i in range(len(config["decode_layers"]) - 1)
+            ],
+            nn.Linear(config["decode_layers"][-1], config["out_dim"]),
+        )
+
+        for m in self.modules():
+            if isinstance(m, (nn.Conv1d, nn.Conv2d)):
+                nn.init.kaiming_normal_(
+                    m.weight, a=0.2, mode="fan_in", nonlinearity="leaky_relu"
+                )
+            elif isinstance(m, (nn.BatchNorm1d, nn.GroupNorm, nn.LayerNorm)):
+                nn.init.constant_(m.weight, 1)
+                if m.bias is not None:
+                    nn.init.constant_(m.bias, 0)
+            elif isinstance(m, nn.Linear):
+                nn.init.xavier_normal_(m.weight)
+                if m.bias is not None:
+                    m.bias.data.zero_()
+
+    def forward(
+        self,
+        x: torch.Tensor,
+        mask: torch.Tensor,
+        env: torch.Tensor = None,
+        idx_base: torch.Tensor = None,
+    ) -> torch.Tensor:
+        """
+        Input:
+                x:      	point set, torch.Size([batch_size, num_dims, num_points])
+                mask:		mask for padding points, torch.Size([batch_size, num_points])
+                env:    	experimental condiction, torch.Size([batch_size, add_num])
+                idx_base:	idx for local knn, torch.Size([batch_size, 1, 1])
+        """
+        if idx_base is None:
+            batch_size, num_dims, num_points = x.size()
+            idx_base = (
+                torch.arange(0, batch_size, device=x.device, dtype=torch.long).view(
+                    -1, 1, 1
+                )
+                * num_points
+            )
+        x = self.encoder(x, idx_base, mask)  # torch.Size([batch_size, emb_dim])
+
+        # add the encoded adduct
+        if self.add_num == 1:
+            x = torch.cat((x, torch.unsqueeze(env, 1)), 1)
+        elif self.add_num > 1:
+            x = torch.cat((x, env), 1)
+
+        # decoder
+        x = self.decoder(x)
+        return x

+#
+# Modified version of mpnn.py
+# Original version available at https://github.com/awslabs/dgl-lifesci/blob/master/python/dgllife/model/gnn/mpnn.py

+
+import torch.nn as nn
+import torch.nn.functional as F
+
+from dgl.nn.pytorch import NNConv
+
+__all__ = ["MPNN"]
+
+
+# pylint: disable=W0221
+class MPNN(nn.Module):
+    """MPNN.
+
+    MPNN is introduced in `Neural Message Passing for Quantum Chemistry
+    <https://arxiv.org/abs/1704.01212>`__.
+
+    This class performs message passing in MPNN and returns the updated node representations.
+
+    Parameters
+    ----------
+    node_in_feats : int
+        Size for the input node features.
+    node_out_feats : int
+        Size for the output node representations. Default to 64.
+    edge_in_feats : int
+        Size for the input edge features. Default to 128.
+    edge_hidden_feats : int
+        Size for the hidden edge representations.
+    num_step_message_passing : int
+        Number of message passing steps. Default to 6.
+    """
+
+    def __init__(
+        self,
+        node_in_feats,
+        edge_in_feats,
+        node_out_feats=64,
+        edge_hidden_feats=128,
+        num_step_message_passing=6,
+        dropout=0.1,
+    ):
+        super(MPNN, self).__init__()
+
+        self.project_node_feats = nn.Sequential(
+            nn.Linear(node_in_feats, node_out_feats), nn.ReLU()
+        )
+        self.num_step_message_passing = num_step_message_passing
+        edge_network = nn.Sequential(
+            nn.Linear(edge_in_feats, edge_hidden_feats),
+            nn.ReLU(),
+            nn.Linear(edge_hidden_feats, node_out_feats * node_out_feats),
+        )
+        self.gnn_layer = NNConv(
+            in_feats=node_out_feats,
+            out_feats=node_out_feats,
+            edge_func=edge_network,
+            aggregator_type="sum",
+        )
+        self.gru = nn.GRU(node_out_feats, node_out_feats)
+        self.dropout = nn.Dropout(dropout)
+
+    def reset_parameters(self):
+        """Reinitialize model parameters."""
+        self.project_node_feats[0].reset_parameters()
+        self.gnn_layer.reset_parameters()
+        for layer in self.gnn_layer.edge_func:
+            if isinstance(layer, nn.Linear):
+                layer.reset_parameters()
+        self.gru.reset_parameters()
+
+    def forward(self, g, node_feats, edge_feats):
+        """Performs message passing and updates node representations.
+
+        Parameters
+        ----------
+        g : DGLGraph
+            DGLGraph for a batch of graphs.
+        node_feats : float32 tensor of shape (V, node_in_feats)
+            Input node features. V for the number of nodes in the batch of graphs.
+        edge_feats : float32 tensor of shape (E, edge_in_feats)
+            Input edge features. E for the number of edges in the batch of graphs.
+
+        Returns
+        -------
+        node_feats : float32 tensor of shape (V, node_out_feats)
+            Output node representations.
+        """
+        node_feats = self.project_node_feats(node_feats)  # (V, node_out_feats)
+        hidden_feats = node_feats.unsqueeze(0)  # (1, V, node_out_feats)
+
+        for _ in range(self.num_step_message_passing):
+            node_feats = F.relu(self.gnn_layer(g, node_feats, edge_feats))
+            node_feats, hidden_feats = self.gru(node_feats.unsqueeze(0), hidden_feats)
+            node_feats = node_feats.squeeze(0)
+            node_feats = self.dropout(node_feats)
+
+        return node_feats

+#

+import torch.nn as nn

+
+from .mpnn import MPNN
+
+__all__ = ["MPNNPredictor"]
+
+
+# pylint: disable=W0221
+class MPNNPredictor(nn.Module):
+    """MPNN for regression and classification on graphs.
+
+    MPNN is introduced in `Neural Message Passing for Quantum Chemistry
+    <https://arxiv.org/abs/1704.01212>`__.
+
+    Parameters
+    ----------
+    node_in_feats : int
+        Size for the input node features.
+    edge_in_feats : int
+        Size for the input edge features.
+    node_out_feats : int
+        Size for the output node representations. Default to 64.
+    edge_hidden_feats : int
+        Size for the hidden edge representations. Default to 128.
+    n_tasks : int
+        Number of tasks, which is also the output size. Default to 1.
+    num_step_message_passing : int
+        Number of message passing steps. Default to 6.
+    num_step_set2set : int
+        Number of set2set steps. Default to 6.
+    num_layer_set2set : int
+        Number of set2set layers. Default to 3.
+    """
+
+    def __init__(
+        self,
+        node_in_feats,
+        edge_in_feats,
+        node_out_feats=64,
+        edge_hidden_feats=128,
+        dropout=0.1,
+        num_step_message_passing=5,
+        num_step_set2set=6,
+        num_layer_set2set=3,
+        n_tasks=1,
+        predictor_hidden_feats=256,
+    ):
+        super(MPNNPredictor, self).__init__()
+
+        self.encoder = MPNN(
+            node_in_feats=node_in_feats,
+            node_out_feats=node_out_feats,
+            edge_in_feats=edge_in_feats,
+            edge_hidden_feats=edge_hidden_feats,
+            num_step_message_passing=num_step_message_passing,
+            dropout=dropout,
+        )
+        self.readout = Set2Set(
+            input_dim=node_out_feats,
+            n_iters=num_step_set2set,
+            n_layers=num_layer_set2set,
+        )
+
+        self.decoder = nn.Sequential(
+            nn.Linear(2 * node_out_feats, predictor_hidden_feats),
+            nn.ReLU(),
+            nn.Linear(predictor_hidden_feats, n_tasks),
+        )
+
+    def forward(self, g, node_feats, edge_feats):
+        """Graph-level regression/soft classification.
+
+        Parameters
+        ----------
+        g : DGLGraph
+            DGLGraph for a batch of graphs.
+        node_feats : float32 tensor of shape (V, node_in_feats)
+            Input node features.
+        edge_feats : float32 tensor of shape (E, edge_in_feats)
+            Input edge features.
+
+        Returns
+        -------
+        float32 tensor of shape (G, n_tasks)
+            Prediction for the graphs in the batch. G for the number of graphs.
+        """
+        node_feats = self.encoder(g, node_feats, edge_feats)
+        graph_feats = self.readout(g, node_feats)
+        output = self.decoder(graph_feats)
+
+        return output

+import os
+import pandas as pd
+import numpy as np
+import json
+from rdkit import Chem, RDConfig, rdBase
+from rdkit.Chem import AllChem, ChemicalFeatures
+
+from util import MANUALLY_REMOVED_SUBSETS, check_metadata
+
+# Disable RDKit logging
+rdBase.DisableLog("rdApp.*")
+
+# Constants for feature extraction
+ATOM_LIST = ["H", "C", "N", "O", "F", "Si", "P", "S", "Cl", "Br", "I"]
+CHARGE_LIST = [1, -1, 0]
+DEGREE_LIST = [1, 2, 3, 4, 0]
+VALENCE_LIST = [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 0]
+HYBRIDIZATION_LIST = ["SP", "SP2", "SP3", "S"]
+HYDROGEN_LIST = [1, 2, 3, 0]
+RINGSIZE_LIST = [3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8]
+BOND_LIST = ["SINGLE", "DOUBLE", "TRIPLE", "AROMATIC"]
+
+
+def determine_thr(x):
+    # x is the rt column of dataframe
+    value_counts = x.value_counts().sort_index()
+    thr = 0
+    pre_single_rt = True
+    count_single_rt = 0
+    for rt, counts in value_counts.items():
+        # print(rt, counts)
+        if counts > 1:
+            thr = rt
+            pre_single_rt = False
+            count_single_rt = 0
+
+        elif counts == 1 and pre_single_rt == True:
+            count_single_rt += 1
+
+        else:
+            pre_single_rt = True
+            count_single_rt = 1
+
+        if count_single_rt > 2:
+            return thr
+
+
+class MolecularPreprocessor:
+    def __init__(self, output_dir="./data", seed=42):
+        self.output_dir = output_dir
+        self.seed = seed
+        self.chem_feature_factory = ChemicalFeatures.BuildFeatureFactory(
+            os.path.join(RDConfig.RDDataDir, "BaseFeatures.fdef")
+        )
+        os.makedirs(output_dir, exist_ok=True)
+
+    def _get_DA_features(self, mol):
+        """Extract donor and acceptor features."""
+        D_list, A_list = [], []
+        for feat in self.chem_feature_factory.GetFeaturesForMol(mol):
+            if feat.GetFamily() == "Donor":
+                D_list.append(feat.GetAtomIds()[0])
+            if feat.GetFamily() == "Acceptor":
+                A_list.append(feat.GetAtomIds()[0])
+        return D_list, A_list
+
+    def _get_chirality(self, atom):
+        """Get chirality features for an atom."""
+        if atom.HasProp("Chirality"):
+            return [
+                (atom.GetProp("Chirality") == "Tet_CW"),
+                (atom.GetProp("Chirality") == "Tet_CCW"),
+            ]
+        return [0, 0]
+
+    def _get_stereochemistry(self, bond):
+        """Get stereochemistry features for a bond."""
+        if bond.HasProp("Stereochemistry"):
+            return [
+                (bond.GetProp("Stereochemistry") == "Bond_Cis"),
+                (bond.GetProp("Stereochemistry") == "Bond_Trans"),
+            ]
+        return [0, 0]
+
+    def _process_stereochemistry(self, mol):
+        """Process and set stereochemistry properties for a molecule."""
+        si = Chem.FindPotentialStereo(mol)
+        for element in si:
+            if (
+                str(element.type) == "Atom_Tetrahedral"
+                and str(element.specified) == "Specified"
+            ):
+                mol.GetAtomWithIdx(element.centeredOn).SetProp(
+                    "Chirality", str(element.descriptor)
+                )
+            elif (
+                str(element.type) == "Bond_Double"
+                and str(element.specified) == "Specified"
+            ):
+                mol.GetBondWithIdx(element.centeredOn).SetProp(
+                    "Stereochemistry", str(element.descriptor)
+                )
+        return mol
+
+    def _process_molecule(self, mol):
+        """Process a single molecule to extract its features."""
+        try:
+            mol = self._process_stereochemistry(mol)
+            assert "." not in Chem.MolToSmiles(mol)
+            mol = Chem.RemoveHs(mol)
+        except:
+            return None
+
+        n_node = mol.GetNumAtoms()
+        n_edge = mol.GetNumBonds() * 2
+
+        D_list, A_list = self._get_DA_features(mol)
+
+        # Atom features
+        atom_features = {
+            "symbol": np.eye(len(ATOM_LIST))[
+                [ATOM_LIST.index(a.GetSymbol()) for a in mol.GetAtoms()]
+            ],
+            "charge": np.eye(len(CHARGE_LIST))[
+                [CHARGE_LIST.index(a.GetFormalCharge()) for a in mol.GetAtoms()]
+            ][:, :-1],
+            "degree": np.eye(len(DEGREE_LIST))[
+                [DEGREE_LIST.index(a.GetDegree()) for a in mol.GetAtoms()]
+            ][:, :-1],
+            "hybridization": np.eye(len(HYBRIDIZATION_LIST))[
+                [
+                    HYBRIDIZATION_LIST.index(str(a.GetHybridization()))
+                    for a in mol.GetAtoms()
+                ]
+            ][:, :-1],
+            "hydrogen": np.eye(len(HYDROGEN_LIST))[
+                [
+                    HYDROGEN_LIST.index(a.GetTotalNumHs(includeNeighbors=True))
+                    for a in mol.GetAtoms()
+                ]
+            ][:, :-1],
+            "valence": np.eye(len(VALENCE_LIST))[
+                [VALENCE_LIST.index(a.GetTotalValence()) for a in mol.GetAtoms()]
+            ][:, :-1],
+            "DA": np.array([[(j in D_list), (j in A_list)] for j in range(n_node)]),
+            "chirality": np.array([self._get_chirality(a) for a in mol.GetAtoms()]),
+            "ring_size": np.array(
+                [[a.IsInRingSize(s) for s in RINGSIZE_LIST] for a in mol.GetAtoms()]
+            ),
+            "aromatic": np.array(
+                [[a.GetIsAromatic(), a.IsInRing()] for a in mol.GetAtoms()]
+            ),
+        }
+
+        node_attr = np.concatenate(list(atom_features.values()), axis=1)
+
+        edge_attr, src, dst = None, None, None
+        if n_edge > 0:
+            bond_features = {
+                "type": np.eye(len(BOND_LIST))[
+                    [BOND_LIST.index(str(b.GetBondType())) for b in mol.GetBonds()]
+                ],
+                "stereo": np.array(
+                    [self._get_stereochemistry(b) for b in mol.GetBonds()]
+                ),
+                "properties": [
+                    [b.IsInRing(), b.GetIsConjugated()] for b in mol.GetBonds()
+                ],
+            }
+
+            edge_attr = np.concatenate(list(bond_features.values()), axis=1)
+            edge_attr = np.vstack([edge_attr, edge_attr])
+
+            bond_loc = np.array(
+                [[b.GetBeginAtomIdx(), b.GetEndAtomIdx()] for b in mol.GetBonds()]
+            )
+            src = np.hstack([bond_loc[:, 0], bond_loc[:, 1]])
+            dst = np.hstack([bond_loc[:, 1], bond_loc[:, 0]])
+
+        return {
+            "n_node": n_node,
+            "n_edge": n_edge,
+            "node_attr": node_attr,
+            "edge_attr": edge_attr,
+            "src": src,
+            "dst": dst,
+        }
+
+    def process_molecules(self, mol_list, label_list):
+        """Process a list of molecules and their labels."""
+        processed_data = {
+            "n_node": [],
+            "n_edge": [],
+            "node_attr": [],
+            "edge_attr": [],
+            "src": [],
+            "dst": [],
+            "label": [],
+        }
+
+        for i, (mol, label) in enumerate(zip(mol_list, label_list)):
+            mol_features = None
+            try:
+                mol_features = self._process_molecule(mol)
+            except Exception as e:
+                print(f"Error processing molecule {i}: {str(e)}")
+                continue
+
+            if mol_features is None:
+                continue
+
+            for key, value in mol_features.items():
+                if value is not None:
+                    processed_data[key].append(value)
+            processed_data["label"].append(label)
+
+            if (i + 1) % 10000 == 0:
+                print(f"--- {i+1}/{len(mol_list)} processed")
+
+        if len(processed_data["label"]) == 0:  # No valid molecules
+            return processed_data
+
+        # Convert lists to arrays
+        for key in processed_data:
+            if key in ["n_node", "n_edge"]:
+                processed_data[key] = np.array(processed_data[key]).astype(int)
+            elif key in ["node_attr", "edge_attr"]:
+                processed_data[key] = np.vstack(processed_data[key]).astype(bool)
+            elif key in ["src", "dst"]:
+                processed_data[key] = np.hstack(processed_data[key]).astype(int)
+            elif key == "label":
+                processed_data[key] = np.array(processed_data[key]).astype(float)
+
+        return processed_data
+
+    def process_SMRT_dataset(self, sdf_path):
+        """Extract METLIN-SMRT (isomeric SMILES + retention time) to ``smrt.csv``.
+
+        The pure-torch TL baseline featurizes SMILES on the fly (via
+        ``timp.models.gnn_features.smiles_to_gnn_graph``, identical features to the RepoRT pool),
+        so only SMILES + RT are needed here --- no offline graph NPZ."""
+        import csv as _csv
+
+        print("\nProcessing METLIN-SMRT dataset...")
+        suppl = Chem.SDMolSupplier(sdf_path, removeHs=False)
+        out = os.path.join(self.output_dir, "smrt.csv")
+        n, rt_min, rt_max = 0, float("inf"), float("-inf")
+        with open(out, "w", newline="") as f:
+            w = _csv.writer(f)
+            w.writerow(["smiles", "rt"])
+            for mol in suppl:
+                try:
+                    Chem.SanitizeMol(mol)
+                    RT = mol.GetDoubleProp("RETENTION_TIME")
+                    if RT > 200:                      # drop non-eluting compounds (dead time)
+                        w.writerow([Chem.MolToSmiles(mol), RT])
+                        n += 1
+                        rt_min, rt_max = min(rt_min, RT), max(rt_max, RT)
+                except Exception:
+                    continue
+        print(f"METLIN-SMRT processed: {n} molecules -> {out}")
+        if n:
+            print(f"RT range: {rt_min:.1f} - {rt_max:.1f}")
+
+    def process_RepoRT_dataset(self, root_dir, threshold):
+        """Process RepoRT dataset."""
+        print("\nProcessing RepoRT dataset...")
+        discarded_record = {
+            "manually_removed": [],
+            "missing_metadata": [],
+            "missing_required_condition": [],
+            "too_few_samples": [],
+            "missing_rt_data": [],
+            "explore": [],
+        }
+        sample_numbers = ""
+
+        subset_list = [
+            f for f in os.listdir(root_dir) if os.path.isdir(os.path.join(root_dir, f))
+        ]
+
+        for subset in subset_list:
+            subset_id = subset.split("_")[0]
+
+            # Filter 1: Check if subset should be excluded
+            if subset_id in MANUALLY_REMOVED_SUBSETS:
+                discarded_record["manually_removed"].append(subset)
+                continue
+
+            # Filter 2: check if the subset has the required columns in metadata
+            metadata_path = os.path.join(
+                root_dir, subset, "{}_metadata.tsv".format(subset)
+            )
+            if not os.path.exists(metadata_path):
+                print("Metadata not found: {}".format(metadata_path))
+                discarded_record["missing_metadata"].append(subset)
+                continue
+            if not check_metadata(metadata_path):
+                print("Missing required columns: {}".format(metadata_path))
+                discarded_record["missing_required_condition"].append(subset)
+                continue
+
+            subset_path = os.path.join(
+                root_dir, subset, f"{subset}_rtdata_isomeric_success.tsv"
+            )
+            if not os.path.exists(subset_path):
+                discarded_record["missing_rt_data"].append(subset)
+                continue
+
+            # Read and process dataset
+            df = pd.read_csv(subset_path, sep="\t")
+            df["smiles"] = df["smiles.std"].apply(
+                lambda x: Chem.MolToSmiles(Chem.MolFromSmiles(x), isomericSmiles=True)
+            )
+            sample_numbers += f"{subset_id}: {len(df)}\n"
+
+            mol_list = [Chem.MolFromSmiles(smiles) for smiles in df["smiles"]]
+            rt_list = df["rt"].tolist()
+
+            # Filter out non-eluting compounds
+            thr = determine_thr(df["rt"])
+            df = df[df["rt"] > thr]
+
+            if len(df) < threshold:
+                discarded_record["too_few_samples"].append(subset)
+                print("Too few samples: {}".format(subset))
+            else:
+                processed_data = self.process_molecules(mol_list, rt_list)
+                np.savez_compressed(
+                    os.path.join(
+                        self.output_dir, f"dataset_graph_report{subset_id}.npz"
+                    ),
+                    data=[processed_data],
+                )
+                discarded_record["explore"].append(subset)
+                print(f'Processed {subset_id}: {len(processed_data["label"])}')
+
+        # Save discarded record
+        with open(
+            os.path.join(self.output_dir, "report_graph_discarded_record.json"), "w"
+        ) as f:
+            json.dump(discarded_record, f, indent=4)
+
+        # Write sample numbers to file
+        with open(
+            os.path.join(self.output_dir, "report_graph_sample_numbers.txt"), "w"
+        ) as f:
+            f.write(sample_numbers)
+
+        print("=" * 20)
+        print("RepoRT Dataset Summary:")
+        for k, v in discarded_record.items():
+            print(f"{k}: {len(v)}")
+        print("=" * 20)
+
+
+def process_CCS_dataset(self, csv_path, threshold=100):
+    """Process METLIN-CCS dataset."""
+    print("\nProcessing METLIN-CCS dataset...")
+    df = pd.read_csv(csv_path)
+
+    # Filter out non-eluting compounds
+    df = df[df["RT"] > 0]
+    if len(df) < threshold:
+        print(f"Dataset has fewer than {threshold} samples. Skipping processing.")
+        return
+
+    mol_list = [Chem.MolFromSmiles(smiles) for smiles in df["SMILES"]]
+    ccs_list = df["RT"].tolist()
+
+    processed_data = self.process_molecules(mol_list, ccs_list)
+    np.savez_compressed(
+        os.path.join(self.output_dir, "dataset_graph_CCS.npz"), data=[processed_data]
+    )
+
+    print(f"CCS dataset processed: {len(ccs_list)} molecules")
+    print(f"CCS range: {min(ccs_list):.1f} - {max(ccs_list):.1f}")
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    import pathlib
+
+    _data_root = pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] / "data"
+    preprocessor = MolecularPreprocessor(
+        output_dir=str(_data_root / "processed_graph"), seed=42
+    )
+
+    # Process METLIN-SMRT dataset (upstream for the conventional-TL baseline) -> smrt.csv
+    _smrt_sdf = _data_root / "SMRT_dataset.sdf"
+    if _smrt_sdf.exists():
+        preprocessor.process_SMRT_dataset(str(_smrt_sdf))
+    else:
+        print(f"[skip] SMRT SDF not found at {_smrt_sdf} (run get_data.sh to download it)")
+
+    # Process RepoRT dataset
+    preprocessor.process_RepoRT_dataset(str(_data_root / 'RepoRT/processed_data'), threshold=100)
+
+    # Process CCS dataset (commented out — CCS not used; process_CCS_dataset is a stray
+    # module-level function, not a class method, and the CCS file is not downloaded)

+    #     str(_data_root / "CCS-Publication-V3/METLIN_IMS_all plot CV %3C2% _dimers.csv"),

+#!/bin/bash
+# Full external-baseline run for Table 5 (tab:baselines_full): extend DNNpwa (ju2021),
+# MDC-ANN (wang2023), and MDL-TL (li2025) to ALL 10 TL-difficult datasets, 5-fold CV, seed 42.
+# Graphormer-RT (stienstra2025) is already complete (baselines/results/summary.csv).
+#
+# Idempotent: skips any (method,target) whose per-fold CSV already holds >=5 fold rows, so the
+# job can be re-launched after an interruption. Results -> baselines/results/{method}_{target}.csv.
+# Pretraining is cached on each baseline's first target, so every baseline loops its targets
+# SEQUENTIALLY; different baselines run concurrently on GPUs 0 and 1.
+set -uo pipefail
+cd /data/yuhhong/TIMPANI
+export PATH=/home/yuhhong/miniconda3/envs/gnn/bin:$PATH
+LOG=baselines/logs; mkdir -p "$LOG" baselines/results
+NW=14
+
+HILIC="report0027 report0183 report0185"
+RP="report0180 report0262 report0263 report0264 report0382 report0401 report0420"
+ALL="$HILIC $RP"
+
+have() { local f="baselines/results/$1_$2.csv"; [ -f "$f" ] && [ "$(wc -l < "$f")" -ge 5 ]; }
+
+run_loop() {  # $1=method  $2=gpu  rest via $ALL ; sequential so pretrain caches once
+  local m="$1" gpu="$2" t
+  for t in $ALL; do
+    if have "$m" "$t"; then echo "[$m] $t already done -> skip"; continue; fi
+    echo "[$m] $t on gpu$gpu start $(date +%H:%M:%S)"
+    if python baselines/$m/run.py -t "$t" --n_folds 5 -s 42 --device "$gpu" >> "$LOG/${m}_${t}.log" 2>&1; then
+      echo "[$m] $t OK $(date +%H:%M:%S)"
+    else
+      echo "[$m] $t FAIL (see $LOG/${m}_${t}.log)"
+    fi
+  done
+}
+
+echo "==================== phase 1: preprocessing (Mordred, CPU) $(date) ===================="
+echo "[pp] ju2021 SMRT + 10 targets"
+python baselines/ju2021/preprocess.py --datasets SMRT $ALL --n_workers $NW > "$LOG/pp_ju.log" 2>&1 \
+  && echo "[pp] ju2021 done $(date)" || { echo "[pp] ju2021 FAILED"; tail -15 "$LOG/pp_ju.log"; }
+echo "[pp] wang2023 SMRT (reference columns) then targets aligned"
+python baselines/wang2023/preprocess.py --datasets SMRT --no_mg --n_workers $NW > "$LOG/pp_wang.log" 2>&1 \
+  && python baselines/wang2023/preprocess.py --datasets $ALL \
+       --align_to baselines/wang2023/data/SMRT_wang2023.npz --no_mg --n_workers $NW >> "$LOG/pp_wang.log" 2>&1 \
+  && echo "[pp] wang2023 done $(date)" || { echo "[pp] wang2023 FAILED"; tail -15 "$LOG/pp_wang.log"; }
+
+echo "==================== phase 2: model runs (GPU 0/1) $(date) ===================="
+# ju2021 -> gpu0, wang2023 -> gpu1 concurrently; then li2025 -> gpu0.
+run_loop ju2021   0 &
+run_loop wang2023 1 &
+wait
+run_loop li2025   0
+
+echo "==================== DONE $(date) ===================="
+echo "Per-target CSVs in baselines/results/. Aggregate with the collector afterwards."

+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# Data-efficiency on report0183 (GIN): SC / TL(SMRT) / TIMPANI(mode-pool) vs. target train size.
+# --subsample_n caps the target TRAIN fold (test untouched); it limits BOTH the Stage-1 anchor and
+# Stage-2 fine-tune (run_timp.py:498). TIMPANI uses the mode-matched pool (deployment-realistic,
+# matching the main benchmark), NOT SMRT-only. Sizes fit 0183's ~92-compound 5-fold train fold;
+# the top point (label 92) is the FULL train fold (subsample_n=0). Results -> results_dataeff/.
+set -uo pipefail
+cd /data/yuhhong/TIMPANI
+export PATH=/home/yuhhong/miniconda3/envs/gnn/bin:$PATH
+OUT=results_dataeff; LOG=baselines/logs; mkdir -p "$OUT" "$LOG"
+EXCL=results_screen/pool_exclusion_mode.json
+DLOG="$LOG/dataeff.log"
+
+sc(){ python scripts/run_timp.py -t report0183 -s 42 --n_folds 5 --device "$2" --backbone gin \
+      --strategy scratch --finetune_epochs 500 --subsample_n "$1" --method_label "sc_n$3" \
+      --results_dir "$OUT" >> "$LOG/de_sc_$3.log" 2>&1; }
+tl(){ python scripts/run_timp.py -t report0183 -s 42 --n_folds 5 --device "$2" --backbone gin \
+      --strategy tl --upstream smrt --finetune_epochs 500 --subsample_n "$1" --method_label "tl_n$3" \
+      --results_dir "$OUT" >> "$LOG/de_tl_$3.log" 2>&1; }
+tp(){ python scripts/run_timp.py -t report0183 -s 42 --n_folds 5 --device "$2" --backbone gin \
+      --strategy timpani --align both --align_meta_batch 4 --meta_steps 4000 --k_support 16 --k_query 16 \
+      --max_per_ds 100 --finetune_freeze_encoder --pool_exclusion "$EXCL" --subsample_n "$1" \
+      --method_label "tp_n$3" --results_dir "$OUT" >> "$LOG/de_tp_$3.log" 2>&1; }
+
+run_size(){ local N="$1" D="$2" L="$3"
+  echo "[$(date +%T)] size $L (subsample_n=$N) gpu$D" >>"$DLOG"
+  sc "$N" "$D" "$L"; tl "$N" "$D" "$L"; tp "$N" "$D" "$L"
+  echo "  OK size $L" >>"$DLOG"; }
+
+echo "[$(date +%F_%T)] dataeff start (0183 GIN; sizes 40 60 80 92-full)" >>"$DLOG"
+{ run_size 40 0 40; run_size 80 0 80; } &     # GPU 0 queue
+{ run_size 60 1 60; run_size  0 1 92; } &     # GPU 1 queue (N=0 -> full train fold, labeled 92)
+wait
+
+python - "$OUT" <<'PY'
+import glob, os, re, sys; sys.path.insert(0, ".")
+from timp.data.evaluate import save_summary
+out = sys.argv[1]; sp = os.path.join(out, "summary.csv")
+if os.path.exists(sp): os.remove(sp)
+seen = set()
+for f in sorted(glob.glob(os.path.join(out, "*_report*.csv"))):
+    m = re.match(r"(.+)_(report\d+)$", os.path.basename(f)[:-4])
+    if not m: continue
+    k = (m.group(1), m.group(2))
+    if k in seen: continue
+    seen.add(k); save_summary(out, m.group(1), m.group(2))
+print("rebuilt", sp, "from", len(seen))
+PY
+echo "[$(date +%F_%T)] dataeff DONE -> $OUT/summary.csv" >>"$DLOG"

+#!/bin/bash
+# GIN experiment batch (review response), all on one GPU (default 0). Idempotent: skips any
+# (label,target) whose per-fold CSV already holds >=5 folds. Results -> results_gin_batch/
+# (ablation + Table-1 ladder) and results_dataeff_big/ (0382/0185 data efficiency).
+#
+#   A. Table-1 ladder: pool-TL (target-agnostic pool pretrain + fine-tune) on all 10, seed 42.
+#   B. Multi-target ablation: full ladder (TL -> pool -> +anchor -> +align) on 4 targets
+#      (0183,0027 HILIC; 0264,0401 RP), seeds 42/43/44.
+#   C. Data efficiency on 0382 (RP, ~386) and 0185 (HILIC, ~145): SC/TL/TIMPANI vs train size.
+set -uo pipefail
+cd /data/yuhhong/TIMPANI
+export PATH=/home/yuhhong/miniconda3/envs/gnn/bin:$PATH
+GPU="${1:-0}"
+LOG=baselines/logs; mkdir -p "$LOG"
+EXCL=results_screen/pool_exclusion_mode.json
+AOUT=results_gin_batch; DOUT=results_dataeff_big; mkdir -p "$AOUT" "$DOUT"
+TP="--align_meta_batch 4 --meta_steps 4000 --k_support 16 --k_query 16 --max_per_ds 100 --finetune_freeze_encoder --pool_exclusion $EXCL"
+
+have() { local f="$1/$2_$3.csv"; [ -f "$f" ] && [ "$(wc -l < "$f")" -ge 6 ]; }   # header + 5 folds
+
+# ---- ladder rungs (results_dir, label, target, seed) ----
+r_tl()     { have "$1" "$2" "$3" && return; python scripts/run_timp.py -t "$3" -s "$4" --n_folds 5 --device "$GPU" --backbone gin --strategy tl --upstream smrt --finetune_epochs 500 --method_label "$2" --results_dir "$1" >> "$LOG/gb_$2_$3.log" 2>&1; }
+r_pool()   { have "$1" "$2" "$3" && return; python scripts/run_timp.py -t "$3" -s "$4" --n_folds 5 --device "$GPU" --backbone gin --strategy timpani --no_target_anchor --align none $TP --method_label "$2" --results_dir "$1" >> "$LOG/gb_$2_$3.log" 2>&1; }
+r_anchor() { have "$1" "$2" "$3" && return; python scripts/run_timp.py -t "$3" -s "$4" --n_folds 5 --device "$GPU" --backbone gin --strategy timpani --align none $TP --method_label "$2" --results_dir "$1" >> "$LOG/gb_$2_$3.log" 2>&1; }
+r_align()  { have "$1" "$2" "$3" && return; python scripts/run_timp.py -t "$3" -s "$4" --n_folds 5 --device "$GPU" --backbone gin --strategy timpani --align both $TP --method_label "$2" --results_dir "$1" >> "$LOG/gb_$2_$3.log" 2>&1; }
+
+ALL10="report0027 report0183 report0185 report0180 report0262 report0263 report0264 report0382 report0401 report0420"
+ABL="report0183 report0027 report0264 report0401"
+
+echo "==================== A. Table-1 pool-TL ladder (all 10, seed 42) $(date) ===================="
+for t in $ALL10; do echo "[A] pool-TL $t $(date +%T)"; r_pool "$AOUT" "poolTL_s42" "$t" 42; done
+
+echo "==================== B. Multi-target ablation (4 targets x 3 seeds) $(date) ===================="
+for t in $ABL; do for s in 42 43 44; do
+  echo "[B] $t seed$s $(date +%T)"
+  r_tl "$AOUT" "tl_s$s" "$t" "$s"
+  r_pool "$AOUT" "pool_s$s" "$t" "$s"
+  r_anchor "$AOUT" "anchor_s$s" "$t" "$s"
+  r_align "$AOUT" "align_s$s" "$t" "$s"
+done; done
+
+echo "==================== C. Data efficiency (0382, 0185) $(date) ===================="
+de(){ local T="$1" N="$2" L="$3"
+  have "$DOUT" "sc_${T}_n$L" "$T" || python scripts/run_timp.py -t "$T" -s 42 --n_folds 5 --device "$GPU" --backbone gin --strategy scratch --finetune_epochs 500 --subsample_n "$N" --method_label "sc_${T}_n$L" --results_dir "$DOUT" >> "$LOG/deb_sc_${T}_$L.log" 2>&1
+  have "$DOUT" "tl_${T}_n$L" "$T" || python scripts/run_timp.py -t "$T" -s 42 --n_folds 5 --device "$GPU" --backbone gin --strategy tl --upstream smrt --finetune_epochs 500 --subsample_n "$N" --method_label "tl_${T}_n$L" --results_dir "$DOUT" >> "$LOG/deb_tl_${T}_$L.log" 2>&1
+  have "$DOUT" "tp_${T}_n$L" "$T" || python scripts/run_timp.py -t "$T" -s 42 --n_folds 5 --device "$GPU" --backbone gin --strategy timpani --align both $TP --subsample_n "$N" --method_label "tp_${T}_n$L" --results_dir "$DOUT" >> "$LOG/deb_tp_${T}_$L.log" 2>&1
+  echo "[C] $T size $L done $(date +%T)"; }
+for pair in "report0382:40:40" "report0382:80:80" "report0382:120:120" "report0382:200:200" "report0382:300:300" "report0382:0:386" \
+            "report0185:40:40" "report0185:80:80" "report0185:120:120" "report0185:0:145"; do
+  IFS=: read -r T N L <<< "$pair"; de "$T" "$N" "$L"
+done
+
+echo "==================== GIN BATCH DONE $(date) ===================="

+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# =============================================================================
+# METADATA-DEGRADATION EXPERIMENT (paper Sec. "Sensitivity to Missing Metadata").
+# Progressively zeroes the target's chromatographic metadata and re-measures GRT+TL.
+# OUTCOME (null, all 10 targets): GRT barely degrades (mean R^2 0.70->0.68 at full
+# removal) and converges to -- does NOT cross below -- the metadata-free GIN+TIMPANI
+# reference. Interpretation: recorded metadata is largely redundant once fine-tuned,
+# which is why TIMPANI matches GRT without it. (Earlier "overtake" hypothesis rejected.)
+# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# GRT's edge assumes clean, complete chromatographic metadata, but RepoRT metadata
+# is frequently missing/inconsistent. We fine-tune + evaluate GRT with an increasing
+# fraction of the TARGET's condition features degraded (missing='zero' or corrupted=
+# 'shuffle'), reusing the SAME clean pretrained mode checkpoints. GIN+TIMPANI (which
+# never uses metadata) is a flat reference line: as degradation rises, GRT decays
+# toward -- and past -- it, giving an honest "why not just use the metadata model?"
+# answer: because you often can't trust the metadata.
+#
+# PREREQ: clean pretrained GRT mode checkpoints must exist
+#   (baselines/stienstra2025/checkpoints/graphormer_pretrain_{rp,hilic}.pt) --
+#   produced by scripts/run_grt_tl_full.sh. This script fine-tunes only (--skip_pretrain).
+# The rate=0 clean baseline is already in baselines/results/stienstra2025_<target>.csv,
+# so this sweeps rates 0.25..1.0. GRT is memory-heavy: ONE run per GPU -> shard by target.
+#
+#   bash scripts/run_grt_meta_robust.sh <GPU> [target ...]      # default 10 TL-difficult
+#   RATES="0.25 0.5 0.75 1.0" MODES="zero" bash scripts/run_grt_meta_robust.sh 0 report0264 &
+#   bash scripts/run_grt_meta_robust.sh 1 report0401 report0420 &
+#
+# Idempotent (skips existing per-target CSVs). Results -> baselines/results/stienstra2025_<mode><pct>_<target>.csv
+# =============================================================================
+set -uo pipefail
+REPO="${TIMPANI_ROOT:-/data/yuhhong/TIMPANI}"
+export PATH="${GNN_BIN:-/home/yuhhong/miniconda3/envs/gnn/bin}:$PATH"
+cd "$REPO"
+
+GPU="${1:-0}"; shift || true
+TARGETS="${*:-report0027 report0183 report0185 report0180 report0262 report0263 report0264 report0382 report0401 report0420}"
+RATES="${RATES:-0.25 0.5 0.75 1.0}"

+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# k (support/query episode size) ablation for TIMPANI. Sweeps k over {8,16,24,32} and measures
+# 5-fold R^2 on a representative subset (2 HILIC + 2 RP difficult targets). Larger k = richer
+# per-task episodes but fewer/larger-only usable tasks (RP 249->74, HILIC 63->7 across the sweep);
+# this measures the NET effect on R^2.
+#
+# For each k it (a) regenerates the condition-rule pool exclusion with min_mols=2k (so small
+# same-condition replicates are caught at small k), and (b) uses an isolated --meta_dir so meta-inits
+# from one k never leak into another. Runs the TIMPANI arm only.
+#   bash scripts/run_k_ablation.sh [gin|grt] [gpu...]     # default: gin, GPUs 0 1 2
+set -uo pipefail
+
+BACKBONE=gin
+if [[ "${1:-}" == "gin" || "${1:-}" == "grt" ]]; then BACKBONE="$1"; shift; fi
+if [ $# -gt 0 ]; then GPUS=("$@"); else GPUS=(0 1 2); fi
+
+KS=(8 16 24 32)
+TARGETS=(report0027 report0183 report0264 report0401)   # 2 HILIC + 2 RP (TL-difficult)
+OUT=results_ablation_k
+LOGDIR=baselines/logs
+mkdir -p "$OUT" "$LOGDIR"
+
+echo "=== regenerating condition-rule exclusion per k ==="
+for k in "${KS[@]}"; do
+  python scripts/compute_pool_exclusion.py --min_mols $((2 * k)) \
+    --out "$OUT/excl_target_k${k}.json" --out_mode "$OUT/excl_mode_k${k}.json" \
+    >> "$LOGDIR/kablation_excl.log" 2>&1 \
+    && echo "  k=${k}: $OUT/excl_mode_k${k}.json" || { echo "  k=${k}: FAILED"; tail -5 "$LOGDIR/kablation_excl.log"; }
+done
+
+run_one() {  # <target> <k> <device>
+  python scripts/run_timp.py -t "$1" -s 42 --n_folds 5 --device "$3" \
+    --backbone "$BACKBONE" --strategy timpani \
+    --align both --align_meta_batch 4 --meta_steps 4000 --k_support "$2" --k_query "$2" \
+    --max_per_ds 100 --finetune_freeze_encoder \
+    --pool_exclusion "$OUT/excl_mode_k${2}.json" \
+    --meta_dir "$OUT/ckpt_${BACKBONE}_k${2}" \
+    --results_dir "$OUT" --method_label "timp_${BACKBONE}_k${2}" \
+    >> "$LOGDIR/kablation_${BACKBONE}_${1}_k${2}.log" 2>&1
+}
+
+# build the (target,k) job list, round-robin across GPUs (sequential per GPU)
+JOBS=()
+for t in "${TARGETS[@]}"; do for k in "${KS[@]}"; do JOBS+=("${t}:${k}"); done; done
+NG=${#GPUS[@]}
+declare -a Q
+for i in "${!JOBS[@]}"; do Q[$((i % NG))]="${Q[$((i % NG))]:-} ${JOBS[$i]}"; done
+
+run_queue() {  # <device> <job...>
+  local D="$1"; shift
+  for J in "$@"; do
+    local T="${J%%:*}" K="${J##*:}"
+    echo "[gpu $D] START $T k=$K $(date +%T)"
+    if run_one "$T" "$K" "$D"; then echo "[gpu $D] OK   $T k=$K $(date +%T)"
+    else echo "[gpu $D] FAIL $T k=$K — see $LOGDIR/kablation_${BACKBONE}_${T}_k${K}.log"; fi
+  done
+}
+
+echo "=== TIMPANI (${BACKBONE}) k-ablation: ${#JOBS[@]} runs on GPUs ${GPUS[*]} ==="
+for gi in "${!GPUS[@]}"; do
+  echo "  gpu ${GPUS[$gi]} <-${Q[$gi]}"
+  run_queue "${GPUS[$gi]}" ${Q[$gi]} &
+done
+wait
+echo "=== DONE. Per-(target,k) CSVs + summary in $OUT/; compare R2 across k (method label timp_${BACKBONE}_k<k>). ==="

+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# =============================================================================
+# PAIRWISE TRANSFER DIAGNOSTIC  (strengthens the paper's headline: fig:motivation)
+# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# The current diagnostic correlates single-source TL R^2 with condition-distance
+# to ONE fixed source (METLIN-SMRT), across ~36 targets. This experiment makes it
+# far stronger: for MANY (source, target) pairs it runs single-source TL from an
+# ARBITRARY RepoRT source dataset (new --upstream single path in run_timp.py) and
+# fine-tunes on the target. Regressing the resulting transfer R^2 on the
+# source->target condition-distance vs. molecular-overlap (analyze_pairwise_diag.py)
+# then shows WITHIN each target that closer-condition sources transfer better --
+# controlling for target difficulty and removing the "it's just SMRT" objection.
+#
+# Sharding: this script pre-trains ONE init per SOURCE and reuses it across all
+# targets, so shard by SOURCE across GPUs (disjoint source lists -> no checkpoint
+# races). Each GPU gets its own meta_dir as a second safety net.
+#
+#   bash scripts/run_pairwise_diag.sh <GPU> [source_id ...]      # default: all sources
+# Example on 4 GPUs (split the 38 sources 4 ways -- see the plan doc):
+#   bash scripts/run_pairwise_diag.sh 0 report0027 report0179 ... &
+#   bash scripts/run_pairwise_diag.sh 1 report0189 report0190 ... &   # etc.
+#
+# Idempotent: skips any (source,target) whose 5-fold CSV already exists.
+# Results -> results_pairwise_diag/  (one CSV per pair: diag_<source>_<target>.csv)
+# =============================================================================
+set -uo pipefail
+REPO="${TIMPANI_ROOT:-/data/yuhhong/TIMPANI}"
+export PATH="${GNN_BIN:-/home/yuhhong/miniconda3/envs/gnn/bin}:$PATH"
+cd "$REPO"
+
+GPU="${1:-0}"; shift || true
+OUT=results_pairwise_diag
+CK="$OUT/ckpt_gpu$GPU"                 # per-GPU meta_dir: source inits never collide across shards
+LOG=baselines/logs
+mkdir -p "$OUT" "$CK" "$LOG"
+
+# All 38 screened RepoRT datasets are candidate sources; the 10 TL-difficult are targets.
+ALL_SOURCES=$(ls data/processed_graph/dataset_graph_report*.npz \
+              | sed -E 's#.*_(report[0-9]+)\.npz#\1#' | sort -u)
+TARGETS="report0027 report0183 report0185 report0180 report0262 report0263 report0264 report0382 report0401 report0420"
+SOURCES="${*:-$ALL_SOURCES}"          # optional CLI source subset for GPU sharding
+
+# single-source pre-train from a small dataset: 2000 steps is plenty (one task); fine-tune as screen.
+PRE="--meta_steps 2000 --k_support 16 --k_query 16 --finetune_epochs 500"
+have(){ local f="$OUT/diag_$1_$2.csv"; [ -f "$f" ] && [ "$(wc -l < "$f")" -ge 6 ]; }
+
+echo "==================== PAIRWISE DIAGNOSTIC (gpu $GPU) $(date) ===================="
+echo "sources: $(echo $SOURCES | wc -w) | targets: $(echo $TARGETS | wc -w)"
+for src in $SOURCES; do
+  for tgt in $TARGETS; do
+    [ "$src" = "$tgt" ] && continue                       # no self-transfer
+    if have "$src" "$tgt"; then echo "[skip] $src -> $tgt"; continue; fi
+    echo "[run ] $src -> $tgt  $(date +%T)"
+    python scripts/run_timp.py -t "$tgt" -s 42 --n_folds 5 --device "$GPU" \
+      --backbone gin --strategy tl --upstream single --source_ds "$src" $PRE \
+      --meta_dir "$CK" --method_label "diag_$src" --results_dir "$OUT" \
+      >> "$LOG/diag_${src}_${tgt}.log" 2>&1 \
+      && echo "   OK $src -> $tgt $(date +%T)" \
+      || echo "   FAIL $src -> $tgt (see $LOG/diag_${src}_${tgt}.log)"
+  done
+done
+echo "==================== PAIRWISE DIAGNOSTIC DONE (gpu $GPU) $(date) ===================="
+echo "Analyze with:  python notebook/analyze_pairwise_diag.py"

+# 0264, 0420) are visible but never individually significant. Repeating CV over
+# many seeds pools S x 5 folds paired points/dataset; with S>=6 the large-effect
+# datasets clear per-dataset p<0.05 and the aggregate tightens well below 0.02.
+#
+# Self-contained: runs TL(SMRT) + TIMPANI for every seed into results_repcv_full/,
+# so it needs nothing copied from the original server. run_timp.py already puts the
+# seed in every checkpoint name, so the isolated --meta_dir never collides.
+#
+#   bash scripts/run_repcv_full.sh <GPU> [seed ...]     # default seeds 42..47 (6 -> 30 pts/dataset)
+# Shard across GPUs by giving each a disjoint seed list:
+#   bash scripts/run_repcv_full.sh 0 42 43 44 &
+#   bash scripts/run_repcv_full.sh 1 45 46 47 &
+#
+# Idempotent; results -> results_repcv_full/.  Analyze with significance_tests.py

+# =============================================================================

+OUT=results_repcv_full; CK="$OUT/ckpt"; LOG=baselines/logs

+T10="report0027 report0183 report0185 report0180 report0262 report0263 report0264 report0382 report0401 report0420"
+have(){ local f="$OUT/$1_$2.csv"; [ -f "$f" ] && [ "$(wc -l < "$f")" -ge 6 ]; }

+        && echo "   OK tl $t s$s" || echo "   FAIL tl $t s$s"

+    fi
+  done
+done

+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# Re-screen all preprocessed RepoRT datasets (>100 compounds) with SC + conventional TL(SMRT)
+# on the pure-torch GIN, to re-identify the TL-difficult set (TL R^2 < 0.8) for the Limitations
+# section under the new backbone. TL pre-trains once on METLIN-SMRT and reuses the checkpoint.
+# Results for EVERY screened dataset (difficult and easy) are saved to results_screen/.
+#   bash scripts/run_screen.sh                 # default: GPUs 0 1 2 (sharded)
+#   bash scripts/run_screen.sh "0 1 2"         # shard across the listed GPUs
+#   bash scripts/run_screen.sh 0               # single GPU
+#   bash scripts/run_screen.sh -1              # CPU
+# Prereq: bash scripts/get_data.sh (SMRT enabled) + python scripts/preprocess_graph.py  -> smrt.csv + NPZs
+set -uo pipefail
+read -r -a GPUS <<< "${1:-0 1 2}"    # space-separated GPU ids -> array
+OUT=results_screen
+LOGDIR=baselines/logs
+CKPT=checkpoints_timp/tl_init_smrt.pt
+mkdir -p "$LOGDIR" "$OUT"
+
+if [ ! -f data/processed_graph/smrt.csv ]; then
+  echo "ERROR: data/processed_graph/smrt.csv missing — run get_data.sh + preprocess_graph.py first." >&2
+  exit 1
+fi
+
+mapfile -t TARGETS < <(ls data/processed_graph/dataset_graph_report*.npz 2>/dev/null \
+                       | sed -E 's#.*dataset_graph_(report[0-9]+)\.npz#\1#' | sort -u)
+if [ ${#TARGETS[@]} -eq 0 ]; then echo "ERROR: no dataset_graph_report*.npz found." >&2; exit 1; fi
+echo "=== screening ${#TARGETS[@]} datasets on GPUs: ${GPUS[*]} (SC + TL-SMRT, GIN) ==="
+
+run() {  # <strategy> <target> <device>
+  python scripts/run_timp.py -t "$2" -s 42 --n_folds 5 --device "$3" \
+    --backbone gin --strategy "$1" --upstream smrt \
+    --meta_steps 4000 --finetune_epochs 500 --results_dir "$OUT" \
+    >> "$LOGDIR/screen_${1}_${2}.log" 2>&1 \
+    && echo "  OK $1 $2 (gpu $3)" || { echo "  FAIL $1 $2 (gpu $3) — see $LOGDIR/screen_${1}_${2}.log"; tail -12 "$LOGDIR/screen_${1}_${2}.log"; }
+}
+
+# Prime the shared SMRT pre-train checkpoint ONCE (first target, first GPU) so the parallel
+# queues below don't race to create it. The first target is fully screened here.
+FIRST="${TARGETS[0]}"
+echo "[$(date +%T)] priming SMRT checkpoint via $FIRST on gpu ${GPUS[0]}"
+run scratch "$FIRST" "${GPUS[0]}"
+run tl      "$FIRST" "${GPUS[0]}"          # creates $CKPT (reused by every tl below)
+[ -f "$CKPT" ] || { echo "ERROR: SMRT pre-train did not produce $CKPT — see $LOGDIR/screen_tl_${FIRST}.log" >&2; exit 1; }
+
+# Shard the remaining targets across GPUs: one sequential queue per GPU, queues run in parallel.
+REST=("${TARGETS[@]:1}")
+NG=${#GPUS[@]}
+queue() {  # <device> <target...>
+  local D="$1"; shift
+  for T in "$@"; do
+    echo "[$(date +%T)] [gpu $D] $T"
+    run scratch "$T" "$D"
+    run tl      "$T" "$D"
+  done
+}
+declare -a Q
+for i in "${!REST[@]}"; do
+  gi=$(( i % NG ))
+  Q[$gi]="${Q[$gi]:-} ${REST[$i]}"
+done
+for gi in "${!GPUS[@]}"; do
+  queue "${GPUS[$gi]}" ${Q[$gi]:-} &        # unquoted: word-split the queue's targets
+done
+wait
+
+# Rebuild summary.csv single-threaded from the safely-written per-target CSVs (parallel
+# save_summary appends could otherwise interleave). Per-target files are the source of truth.
+python - "$OUT" <<'PY'
+import glob, os, re, sys
+sys.path.insert(0, ".")
+from timp.data.evaluate import save_summary
+out = sys.argv[1]
+sp = os.path.join(out, "summary.csv")
+if os.path.exists(sp): os.remove(sp)
+seen = set()
+for f in sorted(glob.glob(os.path.join(out, "*_report*.csv"))):
+    m = re.match(r"(.+)_(report\d+)$", os.path.basename(f)[:-4])
+    if not m: continue
+    key = (m.group(1), m.group(2))
+    if key in seen: continue
+    seen.add(key)
+    save_summary(out, m.group(1), m.group(2))
+print(f"rebuilt {sp} from {len(seen)} (method,target) results")
+PY
+echo "=== DONE. TL-difficult = datasets with tl_gin R2 < 0.8 in $OUT/summary.csv ==="

+"""TIMPANI — driver (Stage 1 target-anchored meta-pretrain + Stage 2 frozen-encoder fine-tune).

+via ``--backbone`` — ``grt`` (Graphormer + chromatography metadata) or ``gin``/``mpnn``/``gat``

+  Stage 1  meta-pretrain a Graphormer-RT init over the RepoRT pool (each dataset = a task).
+           Inner loop adapts the condition context ``z`` (= chrom node) + head on support;
+           outer loop updates the shared encoder + head-base + ChromEncoder on query.

+           the meta-init is target-agnostic and shared across a mode's targets — and never
+           sees the target (leakage gate asserted).

+  Stage 2  adapt to the target. Default recipe (``--align`` set): per-fold target-anchored
+           Stage 1 + frozen-encoder (ANIL) fine-tune (``run_aligned``). Non-aligned path

+def _sample_ep(d, ks, kq):
